bio: Lawrence Alan Agran (born February 2, 1945) is an American lawyer and the current mayor of Irvine, California. Born in Chicago, Agran graduated from UC Berkeley and Harvard Law School. He is the city's longest serving mayor and elected official, having been elected to the city council in 1978.

items.t: Proposed a national health program and funding for local public health clinics in his 1992 presidential campaign.
items.q: "public health clinics, libraries, police forces, and transportation", a national health program, and environmental protections

items.t: Implemented the first city-level ban on CFCs in the country as mayor of Irvine (1989).
items.q: In 1989, Agran implemented the first city-level CFC ban in the country

items.t: Called for zoning and general plan changes to slow suburban sprawl and protect open space (1978).
items.q: Agran's calls for the use of zoning and changes to Irvine's general plan to slow the pace of suburban sprawl and protect open space

items.t: Called for preservation of hillsides and farmlands and was against new freeways in the Irvine area (1986).
items.q: calling for restraints on excessive growth in the city and the preservation of hillsides and farmlands, as well as arguing against new freeways in the Irvine area

items.t: Advocated for withdrawing Irvine from the Transportation Corridor Agencies (1986).
items.q: advocating for the withdrawal of the city from the Transportation Corridor Agencies

items.t: Supervised removal of toxic contamination at the Orange County Great Park site and the building of its features as board chair (2004–2010).
items.q: Agran supervised removal and clean-up of decades of toxic contamination and building of many of the Great Park's iconic features

items.t: Proposed removing all U.S. troops from Western Europe and Japan and redirecting $150 billion as a "peace dividend" to local cities and towns (1992).
items.q: He proposed removing all United States troops from Western Europe and Japan and redirecting 150 billion dollars as a "peace dividend" (1992 value) to local cities and towns for local services

items.t: Established the Local Elected Officials of America project to advocate ending the arms race and reducing U.S. defense spending (1983).
items.q: advocating for municipal priorities that had an international scope, including the end of the arms race, reduction in U.S. defense spending

items.t: Led the Irvine City Council to pass a human rights ordinance prohibiting discrimination, including on the basis of sexual orientation (1988).
items.q: led the Irvine City Council to establish the first human rights ordinance of its kind in Orange County

items.t: Moved to transfer 125 acres of city-owned land to the state for a Veterans Memorial Park and Cemetery; the council passed it unanimously (2014).
items.q: the Irvine City Council unanimously passed Councilmember Larry Agran's motion to transfer 125-acres (50 hectares) of city-owned land

items.t: Co-led a petition initiative to designate the ARDA site as the only site in the Great Park area for cemetery use.
items.q: led by Ed Pope and Larry Agran, to designate by zoning the ARDA site to be the only site in the Great Park area to be used for cemetery purposes

items.t: Supported the use of federal funding for moderate-income housing in Irvine (1978).
items.q: Agran supported increased class integration and the use of federal funding for moderate-income housing in Irvine.

items.t: Argued against Irvine's 2014 term limits measure on the ballot.
items.q: Agran argued against the term limits, calling it the "worst written term limits proposal in history"

items.t: Voted for a new audit of Great Park expenditures, specifying its cost should not exceed $250,000 (2012).
items.q: Agran and the other members of the City Council voted for the new audit, specifying that the cost should not exceed $250,000.
